title: Cash basis to accrual — Rivera Design Studio
instructions: Rivera Design Studio keeps cash-basis records. A lender now requests accrual-basis amounts for Year 2. Convert the amounts using the exhibits, then answer the framework questions.

exhibits.title: Cash-basis summary, Year 2
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Fees collected from clients | 640,000 |
| Salaries paid | 310,000 |
| Rent paid | 48,000 |
| Supplies purchased (cash) | 22,000 |
| Equipment purchased Jan 2 | 50,000 |

exhibits.title: Balance data
exhibits.content:
| Account | Jan 1 | Dec 31 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fees receivable | 58,000 | 75,000 |
| Unearned fees (client retainers) | 12,000 | 20,000 |
| Salaries payable | 9,000 | 14,000 |
| Prepaid rent | 8,000 | 4,000 |
| Supplies on hand | 3,000 | 5,000 |

The equipment has a 5-year life, no salvage, straight-line. No receivables were written off.

rows.label: Appropriate title for Rivera's cash-basis operating statement
options: Statement of revenues collected and expenses paid
Statement of revenues and expenses — income tax basis
rows.answer: Statement of revenues collected and expenses paid
rows.explanation: Cash-basis operating statements use a title that signals cash receipts and payments.

rows.label: If Rivera instead used a modified cash basis, a well-supported modification would be to…
options: Defer fee revenue collected in advance
rows.explanation: Capitalizing and depreciating long-lived assets is a classic modification with substantial support; broad accruals would make it accrual basis.

rows.label: Must the notes quantify the differences between the cash basis and GAAP?
options: No — describe the differences; quantification is not required
rows.answer: No — describe the differences; quantification is not required
rows.explanation: Special purpose frameworks disclose the basis and how it differs from GAAP without having to quantify the effects.
